title: tests/userspace/test_chardev.c: /dev/crypto2dev session lifecycle tests
description:
Userspace test program for /dev/wolfcrypt streaming interface.

Test cases (write/read streaming model):
1. AES-CBC encrypt/decrypt round-trip: open, INIT(cbc(aes), key), SET_IV, write(plain), read(cipher), new fd, INIT(decrypt), SET_IV, write(cipher), read(plain), verify == original
2. AES-GCM encrypt/decrypt with tag: INIT, SET_IV, SET_AAD, write, read, GET_TAG; then decrypt fd: INIT, SET_IV, SET_AAD, SET_TAG, write, read, verify
3. AES-GCM tag tampering: modify tag by 1 bit, decrypt must return -EBADMSG
4. SHA-256: INIT(sha256, HASH), write(data), read(32-byte digest), compare to known vector
5. SHA-256 chunked: same data fed in 64-byte chunks, same digest expected
6. HMAC-SHA256: INIT(hmac(sha256), HASH, key), write, read, compare to known HMAC vector
7. GET_STATE before INIT: initialized==0, algo=="", bytes_written==0
8. GET_STATE after INIT: initialized==1, algo matches what was configured
9. GET_STATE after write+read: bytes_written and bytes_read reflect actual counts
10. 1000 sequential sessions on same fd-per-session pattern
11. 16 concurrent threads, each opens own fd, runs AES-CBC round-trip

Use NIST CAVS vectors from tests/vectors/ for all known-answer checks.
Compile with: gcc -o test_chardev test_chardev.c
design: Each test case: open /dev/wolfcrypt, SESSION_NEW with algorithm+key, CRYPT, SESSION_FREE, close. Use test vectors from hardcoded arrays (same vectors as kernel tests — copy from tests/vectors/*.h). Check every ioctl return value. Report PASS/FAIL per test case. Exit nonzero if any FAIL. See DESIGN.md §test_chardev.
